Balance might mean equal action opportunities, similar winning chances, continued involvement while behind, or several worthwhile approaches. These are related but different goals. Identical dice do not establish identical winning chances, and compensation does not make every choice meaningful.

To compare starting positions, record rolls, choices, and pawn positions alongside the winner. Looking back through the turns helps distinguish a missing final opportunity from earlier setbacks on snakes.

Randomizing the starting player distributes access to that seat before play. It does not remove any advantage the seat may have within a game. Alternating starters across games distributes the role, but does not promise that two outcomes cancel each other out.
Catch-up support needs precise conditions

Consider an unimplemented idea: give the trailing player another option. How is trailing measured: current number, distance to the finish, or chance of winning next turn? Space 8 immediately transfers to 17, while 22 transfers to 12. Comparing unresolved positions can misidentify the state.

Timing also matters. Checking eligibility at the start of a turn differs from checking after movement. An extra die, a reroll, and automatic advancement would change different relationships. None is added to C here; these are questions the proposal must resolve.

Listen to what the trailing player wants. A better chance of winning, or something to do while others act? The first question concerns winning chances; the second concerns attention during a wait. Helping a pawn catch up may not address both.
More players means more than another pawn

A separate three-player C experiment can keep one pawn each, alternating two-dice choices, shared spaces, and immediate victory on exactly 24. The procedure still operates. However, two opponents now act between your turns instead of one, and more people can approach the finish and end the game.

During a three-player test, follow one person between two of their turns. How long do they wait? Can they follow the other pawns? Do they remember what they intended when their turn returns? This shows which part of play the extra person changes.

Resource totals need similar care. In the separate R experiment, two players with two reroll tokens each create four tokens in total. A three-player R trial with the same personal allocation creates six. The table's total grows, but nobody gains more personal rerolls. This remains R, without sharing or transfers, rather than an addition to C.
Try seating a third person

Keep the final candidate at two-player C. If testing with three people, record that count and examine waiting, endings, and explanation demands separately. Changing player count, adding rerolls, and moving snakes together would obscure the cause of any different response.

For a proposed adjustment, name its beneficiary, timing, and intended improvement. Asking whether both players can explain their remaining opportunities after swapping seats produces a more tractable observation than simply asking whether the game is fair.

Make the two-player rules clear, then label the three-player draft separately. When friends sit down, you will know what to watch: how the extra person changes the time between each player’s decisions.
同样退十格，为什么可能讲出不同的故事？
沿蛇从 14 滑到 4，是倒霉地退了十格。把蛇改画成山间滑道，同样从 14 到 4，玩家会不会把它看成一次滑行？先保持基本版 B 的规则，拿两张图试着讲讲这一步，你就开始在做主题设计了。
图像先告诉玩家怎样理解动作
蛇头、蛇尾和梯子的画法，帮助人把跨越很多编号的移动理解为一件事。梯子通向更远的位置，蛇把棋子送回较早的位置，玩家可以用“爬上去了”“掉下来了”来描述数字变化。
“爬上去”和“掉下来”，让人不用每次都重复一串编号。第一次见这张棋盘的人是否也会这样理解，可以请他指一指棋子该去哪儿，再听他怎样描述。
如果用一只非常可爱的蛇，却让它的箭头方向难以辨认，视觉喜好也不能替玩家完成结算。先让人知道发生了什么，才有机会讨论他如何感受。
“贪心受罚”里，玩家真的选过吗
在B版中，落到14是单骰结果和位置共同决定的，玩家没有选择是否冒险。若规则旁边写“因为你贪心，所以受到惩罚”，故事便把一个未曾作出的决定安到了玩家身上。
我们可以把它写成意外，也可以在另一个版本中真的提供风险选择，再讨论这个选择怎样被讲述。重点不是禁止带有情绪的语言，而是让语言与可做的行动相符。否则，玩家可能理解剧情，却仍不知道自己刚才到底能改变什么。
选择版 C 虽然能选骰，也要看玩家有没有看懂两个去处。漏看蛇头和主动冒险，可能得到同一个坏落点，却讲不成同一种故事。
主题可以帮助记住关系，也会增加承诺
假设我们把四个转移都解释成山路：3到11、8到17是上坡捷径，14到4、22到12是滑落。地图可以用统一的箭头和起终点编号支持这个设定，而无需增加新的移动规则。初次体验的人是否因此更容易找到去向，需要实际试读。
若标题改成“登山救援”，玩家可能进一步期待能帮助落后的同伴。但当前C版只有个人先到终点获胜，没有救援动作，也不要求共同到达。标题一旦邀请了新的关系，规则就要承担相应的承诺，或把表述收回到实际能够发生的事。
主题文字也有出场时机。选骰时，一句“落在蛇头，滑到蛇尾”比一段身世更容易查。长故事可以放在开局前或游戏之外，让玩家想读时再读。
让同一步移动换一种说法
准备两张仅改变图像与措辞的纸面局部图，保留14到4的规则，请参与者指出棋子该移到哪里，再用自己的话说发生了什么。随后询问他对这一步的感受。操作是否正确、怎样叙述、是否喜欢，应分开记录。
记下参与者使用的词：他说“被罚了”“滑下来了”，还是只说“回到 4”？这些说法能帮助你调整下一张图和旁边的句子。若两张图讲出的意思很接近，也值得留下这个结果。
我们的交付稿暂时仍叫《二十四格小赛跑》，用蛇与梯子提示移动。给自己的草稿加主题时，也可以先挑这样一个动作来做。看看图像、文字和玩家实际做的事，能不能讲到一起。
Why might the same setback tell a different story?

Sliding down a snake from 14 to 4 can feel like an unlucky loss of ten spaces. Redraw the snake as a mountain slide, with the same endpoints: might someone describe the move as a ride downhill? Keep base version B’s rules and try describing the step with each picture. You are beginning to work on theme.
Pictures suggest how to understand an action

Heads, tails, and ladders help players understand a transfer across many numbered spaces as an event. A ladder leads farther along; a snake returns a pawn to an earlier position. People can describe the numerical change as climbing or falling.
“Climb up” and “slide down” spare people from repeating a string of space numbers. Ask someone new to the board to point out the destination, then listen to how they describe getting there.
An appealing snake illustration still needs a readable direction. Recognizing what happened is a starting point for discussing how it felt.
“Punished for greed”—did the player choose a risk?

In B, landing on 14 follows from the pawn's position and a single die. The player did not choose to take a risk. A caption saying they were punished for greed would attribute a decision that never occurred.

We could describe the event as an accident, or develop a different version that offers an actual risk decision. The aim is to align language with available actions. Otherwise, a player may understand the fiction while remaining unsure what they could have changed.
Even in choice version C, check whether the player understood both destinations. Missing a snake head and deliberately taking a risk can produce the same bad landing, but tell different stories.
Theme can clarify relationships and create promises

Imagine describing the four transfers as mountain paths: 3 to 11 and 8 to 17 are uphill shortcuts; 14 to 4 and 22 to 12 are slides. Consistent arrows and endpoint numbers can support that fiction without adding movement rules. Whether it helps a new reader locate destinations remains a question for a reading test.

A title such as “Mountain Rescue” might also suggest helping a trailing companion. Current C offers no rescue action and rewards an individual arrival first. If the title promises that relationship, the rules need to support it, or the description needs adjusting.

Theme text also needs a place and a time. While choosing a die, “land on the head, slide to the tail” is easier to consult than a character’s life story. Longer stories can sit before play or alongside it, available when someone wants to read them.
Describe the same move another way

Prepare two local paper diagrams that change only the image and wording, keeping the 14-to-4 rule. Ask participants to show the movement, describe what happened, and then discuss their response. Record correct operation, interpretation, and preference separately.

Note the words people use: “I was punished,” “I slid down,” or simply “back to 4.” Those descriptions can help you revise the next picture and its caption. If both pictures prompt much the same account, keep that finding too.

Our handoff keeps the title The 24-Space Race and uses snakes and ladders to explain movement. When adding a theme to your own draft, start with one action like this. See whether the picture, the words, and what the player does tell a consistent story.
谁在跑，谁在赢，谁在讲这个故事？
试着按这个序列走选择版 C：从 0 掷出两个 3，选一颗，登梯子到 11；下一回合又是两个 3，落在 14，滑回 4；再掷出两个 4，选一颗，沿 8 的梯子到 17。双数始终只走一次。把这段人为排出的过程讲给朋友听，你也许会说：“先冲上去，摔下来，又爬了上去。”
故事可以从一连串规则后果里长出来
规则没有写好这三幕剧情，也没有要求玩家抽一张“逆境重生”的故事卡。位置的变化、接近终点的目标，以及人对先后发生之事的回忆，已经提供了可讲述的材料。
讲述时，棋盘能帮你核对到过哪里：11、4、17。要说“追上了别人”，还得补上其他棋子的位置；要说“终于松了口气”，则要听玩家自己的感受。好故事的细节，可以在真实的一局里找。
有些局面曲折，有些很平淡。设计者可以安排会产生起伏的连接，至于哪一段被玩家记住，要等他们玩完以后讲给你听。
比赛里的领先者，不一定是玩家的胜利者
《骆驼大赛》（Camel Up）第二版提供了一个有用的对照。Lookout 2024年重印规则的印刷第3页说明，五匹竞赛骆驼不属于任何玩家；玩家对赛况下注，最终以金钱多少决定胜负。移动一匹骆驼时，还会带走叠在它上面的骆驼。
摆一个不涉及观众板块或逆行骆驼的局部例子：黄骆驼在蓝骆驼上方，蓝骆驼的骰子被揭示，蓝前进时也载着黄一起走。触发这次动作的人、被移动的棋子、因先前判断而可能获益的人，并不需要是同一个人。
对比我们的C版，“我的棋子先准确到24，就是我赢”把这几种关系紧密连在一起；《骆驼大赛》把它们拆开了。因此竞速设计可以把选择放在如何看比赛、何时承诺判断、怎样影响公共赛况，而不局限于怎样开动自己的棋子。
谁行动，谁受益
研究一个案例时，先写下发生了什么，再写谁有权决定，以及收益给谁。在刚才的叠骆驼局部例子中，移动规则产生连带后果；哪位玩家因此更接近获胜，还取决于各自已有的下注与金钱，不能只看谁的手碰了金字塔。
拿一张赛道草图试想：棋子如果不属于任何人，大家会凭什么关注它？先在玩家名字旁写一个目标，再把会影响那个目标的移动连过去。这是一张构思图，暂时不改选择版的规则。
我们的纸上赛跑让“一人一枚棋子”保持清楚，方便初学者追踪结果。《骆驼大赛》则提醒你，等想研究另一种参与方式时，可以从人与棋子的关系改起。
游戏中的因果，不会自动成为现实的证据
我们的蛇梯棋变体可以研究准确落点如何影响前进，却不能证明现实中成功主要靠运气。《骆驼大赛》的叠放关系能产生连带移动，也不能拿来解释真实动物的比赛行为。规则选择了哪些关系，就让哪些关系在这个人工世界里发生。
若想制作有现实主题的模型，需要另行核验：省略了什么，哪些参数只是方便游玩，哪些关系有外部依据。玩家从模型得到的解释，还要与模型实际能支持的范围对照。
回到开头的三次移动，试写一段简短的赛况，再逐句核对：哪些能在棋盘上指出来，哪些需要询问玩家，哪些已经在谈棋盘之外的世界。这样修改以后，故事可以生动，读者也知道细节从哪里来。
Who is racing, who is winning, and who tells the story?

Try this sequence in choice version C. From 0, roll two 3s, choose one, and climb to 11. On the next turn, two more 3s land you at 14 and send you down to 4. Two 4s then let you reach the ladder at 8 and climb to 17. Doubles always give one move. Tell a friend about this arranged sequence and you might say, “I climbed, fell, then climbed again.”
A sequence of consequences can become a story
No rule scripted these three scenes or required a comeback story card. Changing positions, an objective at the finish, and a person's memory of events already provide material for a narrative.

The board lets you check the destinations in that account: 11, 4, 17. To say you caught another player, you would also need their position. To describe relief, you would need to hear how the player felt. A real game is where those details can be found.
Some turns form a dramatic sequence; others are quiet. A designer can arrange connections that produce reversals. Which passage people remember is something to hear from them after play.
The leading racer need not be the winning player

Camel Up, Second Edition supplies a useful contrast. Printed page 3 of Lookout's 2024 reprint rules explains that its five racing camels belong to no player. Players bet on the race and win through money. A moving camel carries the camels stacked above it.

Construct a local position without spectator tiles or crazy camels: yellow sits above blue, and blue's die is revealed. Blue's movement also carries yellow. The person triggering the action, the piece moving, and the person who may benefit from an earlier judgment need not coincide.

C closely links those relationships: my pawn reaching exactly 24 first wins for me. Camel Up separates them. Racing design can locate decisions in observing, committing to a prediction, or influencing a shared event, rather than only moving a personal pawn.
Who acts, and who benefits?

When studying a case, distinguish what happens, who has authority to decide, and who receives a benefit. Carrying another camel creates a linked movement consequence. Which player becomes closer to victory also depends on existing bets and money, not just whose hand touched the pyramid.

Take a sketch of a track and imagine that no one owns its pawns. Why would each player care about them? Write a goal beside each player’s name and draw a line to movements that could affect it. This is a sketch for a new idea; the choice version’s rules stay as they are.

Our paper race keeps one pawn per person so a beginning designer can follow actions and results. Camel Up shows another place to start when you want to explore participation: change how people relate to the pieces.
Rules consequences are not evidence about the world

Our Snakes and Ladders variant can show how exact landing affects progress. It cannot establish that real-world success mostly depends on luck. Camel Up's stacking produces linked movement without explaining actual animal behavior. Each artificial world implements the relationships its rules select.

A model intended to address reality needs further investigation: what was omitted, which parameters merely make play manageable, and which relationships have outside evidence? Interpretations should remain within what the model supports.

Return to the three moves at the opening and write a short account of the race. Check each sentence: can you point to it on the board, would you need to ask a player, or does it make a claim about the world outside the game? The revised story can keep its interest while showing where its details come from.
两颗骰子放在桌上，规则怎样让人只走一次？
还记得 6 上的 2 和 6 吗？按选择版 C，选 2 可以登梯子到 17。现在故意把两颗相加试试：从 6 走八格，落到 14，反而滑回 4。只差一个“选”字，一回合就朝相反的方向走了。
把重要区别放在操作发生的地方
只在第一页写“选择一个结果”可能还不够。两颗骰子挨在一起，容易让人想到相加。可以在规则卡上写“掷两颗，选一颗，只移动一次”，再给选中的骰子画一个放置框；未选中的放到旁边。
这个摆放框没有添加新行动，只让已作出的选择留在桌面。别人能够看见用的是哪一颗，玩家数到一半也能回头核对。若使用两个相同点数，仍只选一颗、移动一次，不额外前进。
解释文字也要贴近使用位置。骰子旁说明怎么选，梯子旁说明转移去向，终点旁说明准确到达。将所有细节集中在远处一大段文字里，可能让玩家知道规则存在，却难在需要时找到。
让文字和棋盘按同一顺序说话
这一回合可以读成一条短流程：看两颗骰子，选一颗；计算从当前格前进后的落点；若超过24，留在回合开始位置并结束；否则移动到落点，执行那里的一次蛇或梯子转移；准确到24则立即获胜。
棋盘中的四条转移，终点都没有再接另一条转移。因此读者不需要猜测是否连跳。经过第8格不会登梯，只有最终落在8才去17；到17后也不能再倒着爬回8。把这些区别放在一张局部图上，比把每一种误会都写成长段警告清楚。
再检查第23格、骰面2和6的局面。两种选择都超过24，棋子留在23，这次行动结束；不会弹回、不会重掷、不会因为两颗都不合适而获得额外回合。没有写出的补救不能靠现场临时商量替代。
组件帮助记忆，不应只靠颜色传话
让每条转移同时具有起点编号、终点编号和方向箭头。蛇与梯子可以有不同图像，但不能仅靠红色与绿色区别作用。两枚玩家棋子也可增加不同形状，帮助辨认谁停在哪里。
24的终点标记应与普通格不同，却仍保留数字。起点0在编号1到24之外，避免有人把放在1的棋子当作已经前进了一步。同格允许两枚棋子并排站，格子大小也要实际容得下，而不是让拥挤的组件暗示“这里只有一个位置”。
把说明放到棋盘旁，亲手走一遍。读到“选一颗”时，有没有地方放选中的骰子？读到“同格”时，格子容不容得下两枚棋子？这些地方对得上，材料才会帮你解释规则。
先请人做一回合，再看哪里需要解释
准备棋盘、两颗骰子和简短规则卡，摆出第 6 格与 2、6，请读者完成一次移动。记下他选了哪颗、从哪格开始数、有没有执行梯子，以及哪一步停下来求助。
若发生错误，先找它出现的位置。把骰子相加，可能需要强调选择；已经选2却仍走到12，可能是数格过程的问题；落8却不去17，则需要检查转移提示。不要把所有错误都归成“没有认真读”。
一次先改最影响操作的一处提示，再让人试同一个任务。等这一回合说得清楚了，再用第 27 章的完整规则，请没听过讲解的人从摆棋开始试。你现在修好的骰子框、箭头和终点说明，都能带到那张规则纸上。
With two dice on the table, how do the rules produce one move?

Remember the 2 and 6 beside a pawn on 6? Choice version C lets you choose 2 and climb to 17. Now deliberately add the dice: eight steps from 6 land at 14 and send you back to 4. One missed instruction to choose can send the turn in the opposite direction.
Put the distinction where the action happens

Writing “choose a result” on the opening page may be insufficient. Two dice placed together can suggest addition. A short reminder can say: “Roll two. Choose one. Move once.” A drawn box for the selected die, with the other placed aside, makes the choice visible.

The box adds no new action. It preserves a decision so another person can check the result used, or the player can recover their place while counting. Doubles still mean selecting one die and moving once, without a bonus.

Locate information near its use: choice beside the dice, destination beside the ladder, and exact arrival beside the finish. A distant block of complete rules may be difficult to consult at the relevant moment.
Let the text and board explain the same sequence

The turn has a short procedure: inspect both dice and select one; calculate the destination from the current position; if it exceeds 24, stay at the turn's starting position and end; otherwise move and apply that space's snake or ladder transfer. Reaching exactly 24 wins immediately.

None of the four transfer destinations starts another transfer. Readers need not guess about chains. Passing through 8 does nothing; landing there moves the pawn to 17, without permitting a return climb. A local diagram can show these distinctions more clearly than a lengthy list of possible misunderstandings.

Check a second position: space 23 with results of 2 and 6. Both overshoot, so the pawn stays on 23 and the turn ends. There is no bounce, reroll, or bonus turn because neither result fits. Improvising a rescue at the table would change the rules.
Components should not communicate through color alone

Give each transfer a starting number, destination number, and directional arrow. Snakes and ladders may use different pictures, but their meaning should not depend only on red versus green. Distinct pawn shapes can also help identify players.

Make the finish visually distinct while retaining 24. Place the starting area 0 outside numbered spaces 1–24, avoiding uncertainty about whether a pawn on 1 has already moved. Allow enough room for two pawns to share a space, so physical crowding does not imply exclusive occupation.

Place the instructions beside the board and use them. At “choose one,” is there somewhere to put the selected die? At “share a space,” can both pawns fit? Matching these details helps the materials explain the rules.
Observe one turn before revising the explanation

Prepare the board, two dice, and a short rule card. Set out the pawn at 6 with results of 2 and 6, then ask a reader to move. Note which die they choose, where they begin counting, whether they use the ladder, and where they pause to ask for help.

Locate any error before explaining it. Adding dice may require a stronger choice cue. Selecting 2 but reaching 12 may concern counting. Landing on 8 without transferring may concern the arrow. Do not reduce all mistakes to careless reading.

Change the cue that most affects the task, then try that task again. Once this turn reads clearly, use the complete rules in chapter 27 with someone who has not heard your explanation, starting from setup. The die box, arrows, and finish reminder you refine here can all go on that rule sheet.
看懂了选择，就一定能参与吗？
想象小雨看着两颗骰子，已经想好要选 2，却够不到棋盘另一侧的棋子。小林伸手帮忙：“6 大，当然走 6。”棋子挪好了，小雨的决定却没被执行。
从看清局面到移动棋子，中间有好几步。这个片段里的小雨需要别人帮她够到棋子，选哪颗骰子的事，她已经想清楚了。
先找到被挡住的是哪一步
我们使用两骰择一版 C：两人轮流掷两颗骰子，选一颗移动，只有落点才触发蛇或梯子。小雨在第 6 格时选 2，会落到 8，再升到 17；选 6 则停在 12。她已理解这段关系，困难只是够不到棋子。让她指认目的地、由同伴按她的决定移动，是一种可比较的支持方式。
如果困难在看清梯子，代拿棋子就没有解决问题。如果她把两个点数相加，可能需要检查动作提示；如果她理解规则却不愿解释理由，也不能自动判断她没学会。设计者应先写出发生困难的具体任务，再决定调整什么。
不让一种线索承担全部工作
两枚棋子若只有红绿差别，在某些光线、视力条件或印刷方式下可能难分。可以同时使用不同形状，并在玩家面前放相同的形状标记。梯子用连续横档连接，蛇用另一种曲线和向下箭头，起点、终点与关键数字也用文字或符号说明。
把材料真的摆到桌上，看看加大的数字有没有挤住路线，新增的图标是否容易认。请人找一次 8 到 17 的连接，比只问哪张图漂亮更能检查这个任务。黑白打印也值得试，它能暴露只靠颜色传话的地方；实际使用还要听不同参与者的反馈。
改变操作，还是改变游戏？
难以抓握骰子时，可以由同伴代掷，让玩家保留选骰权。也可以尝试六张数字卡每次抽一张、看完放回再混匀，连续做两次，作为另一种结果发生器。它只有在每个数字等可能、每次放回且两次独立的假设下，才与两颗公平六面骰的概率模型一致。忘记放回，就已经改变了随机机制。
另一种提案是直接让玩家报一个 1 到 6 的数。它当然方便操作，却把随机结果改成自由选择，不能作为规则不变的支持方式来解释。这样的新游戏也可以研究，只是需要另立版本，重新检查选择与难度。
先问对方想怎么做
《蜗牛赛跑》20629 让六只蜗牛全部参加，玩家猜谁先到、谁最后到，不各自控制一只。这提供了另一种参与办法：可以一起观察和预测。借来设计时，仍要问眼前的人愿不愿意做这件事。
邀请时，可以直接说：“够不到的话，你指给我，我按你说的移。想换一种办法也可以。”同时说明随时能暂停或停止。记录时，把“同伴代移棋子”和“同伴选了点数”分开写；回看这段过程，才能知道帮助有没有保住玩家想做的决定。
Can you make the choice you understand?

Imagine Yu looking at the dice. She wants the 2, but cannot reach her pawn on the far side of the board. Lin reaches over to help: “Six is bigger; take the six.” The pawn has moved, but Yu’s decision has not been followed.
Several steps sit between reading a position and moving a pawn. In this scene, Yu needs help reaching the piece. She has already decided which die to use.
Locate the task that is difficult

We are using choice version C: two players alternate turns, rolling two dice and choosing one for a single move. Only landing triggers a snake or ladder. From 6, Yu’s 2 reaches 8 and climbs to 17; the 6 stops at 12. She understands the difference. Letting her point to the destination while someone moves the piece would address the difficulty she has.

If the difficulty is seeing a ladder, moving the pawn for someone does not solve it. If the player adds the dice, the action reminder may need work. A player who understands the rule but does not want to explain their reasoning has not necessarily failed to understand. Describe the specific task before proposing a solution.
Give important information more than one cue

Pawns distinguished only by red and green may be difficult to tell apart under some visual, lighting, or printing conditions. Distinct shapes, with a matching shape beside each player, offer another cue. Ladder rungs, a different curved path for snakes, directional arrows, and clear labels can distinguish transfers without relying entirely on color.

Put the materials on the table and check whether larger numbers crowd the route or extra symbols are easy to recognise. Ask someone to find the connection from 8 to 17. That checks the task more directly than asking which board looks prettier. A grayscale print is also useful for finding information carried by colour alone; feedback from people using the materials still matters.
Change the operation, or change the game?

If grasping dice is difficult, a companion can roll while the player keeps the choice of result. Another proposal uses six numbered cards: draw one, replace it, mix, and repeat. This matches the probability model of two fair six-sided dice only under explicit assumptions: equally likely numbers, replacement every time, and independent draws. Forgetting replacement changes the mechanism.

Letting someone simply name a number from 1 to 6 may be easier to operate, but replaces a random result with a free choice. That can be an interesting new game. It should receive its own version and a fresh examination of decisions and difficulty, rather than being described as an unchanged way to operate C.
Ask how the player wants to do it

Snail’s Race 20629 uses all six snails, with players predicting the first and last finishers rather than controlling one each. It offers another way to participate: watching and predicting together. If you borrow that approach, ask whether the people at your table want to do that task.

An invitation can be direct: “If the piece is out of reach, point to where you want it and I’ll move it. We can try another way too.” Explain that pausing or stopping is always possible. In your notes, separate a companion moving the pawn from a companion choosing the number. That distinction lets you check whether the help preserved the player’s decision.
一张小棋盘，先回答哪一个问题？
你可以花一个下午画漂亮的蛇，也可以先画两个箭头：8 到 17，14 到 4。哪一个更合适，取决于此刻想知道什么。如果问题是读者能否理解“只有停下才触发梯子”，精致的蛇鳞暂时不会提供答案。
先挑一个要检查的动作，再准备能让人做出它的材料。这份材料就是眼下的原型。它可以很粗糙，但不能把回答问题所需的部分一起省掉。
这次先看玩家会不会选骰
“加上选择以后，会不会更好玩？”包含很多问题。玩家能否看清两个结果，是否注意到梯子，比较时等了多久，输赢时是否愿意继续，都不是同一种观察。本次先问：第一次看见 C 版的人，能否知道两颗骰子只选一颗，并分别结算两个候选点数？
设置同一个局面：棋子在 6，骰子显示 2 和 6。保留完整的 24 格编号与四处蛇梯连接；给出 C 版操作提示，让参与者选一次并移动。不要先告诉他们选 2 更远。如果有人选 6 后正确走到 12，他们可能理解规则，只是没有采用我们偏好的选择。
固定结果，是为了检查关系
直接摆出 2 和 6，省下等待这个组合出现的时间。换一张提示卡或梯子图时，仍然摆同样的结果，就能比较不同材料怎样解释同一个动作。
这个小任务适合查说明。要知道一局中多久出现一次值得考虑的选择，或玩家是否喜欢整个节奏，还要另约一次完整游玩。把这两件事分开，你就不用逼一张局面图回答整款游戏的问题。
删掉什么，不能删掉什么
本次不用重掷标记，不用补给格，也不需要把合作实验放进来。它们分别属于 R、E 和 S，会增加别的问题。为了检查落点，至少要看清起点 6、候选经过的位置、梯底 8 和梯顶 17；为了防止读者误以为这是整套棋盘，仍应标明它是完整棋盘的一次局面示例。
如果只剪下 6、8、17 三张纸，让 6 直接连到 8，可能把走两格误教成一次跳跃。删除组件之后，必须检查关系有没有被一起删除。原型简单，是让一个问题清楚，不是让规则靠主持人口头补齐。
在记录纸上留好位置
留出“选了哪颗”“走到哪里”“在哪儿停下来”三栏。如果有人相加两颗骰子，记在动作栏，再检查提示；如果经过 8 时爬梯，就圈出那个落点，回头看触发说明。先能找到出错的位置，修改才有着落。
也给没想到的做法留一块空白。你准备的解释只是为了更容易观察，朋友可能带来另一种读法。拿着这张记录纸和棋盘，就可以安排第一次试用了。
What should one small board answer first?

You could spend an afternoon drawing beautiful snakes, or begin with two arrows: 8 to 17 and 14 to 4. Which is useful depends on the current question. If you want to know whether someone understands that only landing activates a ladder, detailed scales will not yet supply the answer.
Choose an action to check, then make the materials someone needs to carry it out. That is the prototype for now. It can be rough, provided the parts needed to answer the question are still there.
Start by checking the die choice

“Is it more fun with a choice?” contains several questions. Seeing both outcomes, noticing the ladder, taking time to compare, and wanting another game after losing require different observations. Begin with one: can someone new to C understand that two rolled dice offer one selected move, and work out each candidate result?

Set the pawn on 6 and the dice to 2 and 6. Keep the full 24-space numbering and all four transfers. Provide the C action reminder, then ask the participant to choose and move. Do not announce that the 2 travels farther. Someone who chooses 6 and correctly moves to 12 may understand the rules perfectly, even without making the choice we expected.
Fix the result to examine the relationship

Setting out 2 and 6 saves waiting for that roll to happen. When you change a reminder card or ladder drawing, use the same results again. You can then compare how the materials explain the same action.

This small task is useful for checking instructions. To learn how often a game offers an interesting choice, or whether players enjoy its pace, arrange a separate full game. Keeping those tasks apart stops one position diagram from having to answer for the entire design.
What can be removed, and what must remain?

This test needs no reroll tokens, replenishment space, or cooperative deadline. Those belong to R, E, and S and introduce other questions. Understanding a landing requires seeing space 6, the intervening spaces, ladder base 8, and ladder top 17. Label the material as one situation on a complete board, rather than implying that this fragment is the entire game.

Cutting out only cards marked 6, 8, and 17 might accidentally teach the advance from 6 to 8 as a single jump. After removing a component, inspect whether its relationship disappeared too. A simple prototype should clarify a question, not depend on the facilitator silently filling missing rules.
Make room on the recording sheet

Leave columns for the die selected, the destination reached, and any pause. If someone adds the dice, record the action and check the cue. If they climb while passing 8, circle that position and review the trigger instruction. Finding where the difficulty occurs gives the revision somewhere to start.

Leave space for something you did not anticipate. Your possible explanations help you watch, but a friend may read the materials another way. With this sheet and the board, you can arrange the first try.
怎样安排一次不会问散的试玩？
“来帮我玩一下，看看好不好玩。”朋友坐下以后，这句话仍没有说清你准备观察什么。对方可能评价画面，可能努力赢，也可能为了照顾你而不说困惑。一次小测试需要一个双方都能理解的任务。
拿上一章的棋盘来约一次小测试。这次只看一个新接手的人，能否靠纸上的说明选一颗骰子，把棋子移到该去的地方。
让材料与问题相配
准备同一版的 24 格棋盘、两枚棋子、两颗普通六面骰和 C 版说明。为检查那个具体问题，先摆成棋子在 6、骰子为 2 与 6 的状态，明确告诉参与者这是预设局面。请他们阅读后选一个结果并移动，不要先演示正确答案。
如果改为让大家从 0 开始玩完整一局，就可能一直遇不到这个组合。完整游戏能够回答节奏与持续参与的问题，却不保证展示我们此刻要检查的规则。测试范围改变时，任务和记录方式也要跟着改变。
先说明可以怎样求助
可以这样邀请：“能帮我看看这张说明好不好用吗？先试着按纸上写的走一回合。有不清楚的地方就问，随时可以停，我会记下哪里需要补充。”同时说清准备怎样记录；如果想公开原话或照片，另外征得同意。
需要帮助时就帮忙。先记下对方停在哪儿，再写自己说了什么，以及对方随后怎样做。这样回看记录时，就分得清哪些是材料解释清楚的，哪些还需要你在旁边。
把观察表留给真正发生的事
先写版本 C、预设位置 6、点数 2 和 6、说明是否提前讲解、参与者是否见过本棋盘。空白栏留给实际选择、移动路线、查看哪一处文字、提问和主持提示。若想了解想法，可以在动作后问“刚才你怎样决定的？”而不是问“你是不是没看见梯子？”
“刚才怎么选的”把解释留给对方；“是不是没看见梯子”则已经给了他一个答案。听完后把原话与移动记在一起。没记清的地方标出来，别为了笔记整齐而补出细节。
比较两份材料时，别忘记人也在学习
假如要比较两种梯子画法，先固定规则和局面，只换图形。让同一个人连续看 A、B 两张图，第二次可能因为已经知道答案而更顺利。如果有多位愿意参加的人，可以交替安排先看哪张；人数很少时也应保留顺序记录，而不是声称已经排除了学习影响。
检查一遍桌上的东西：同一版材料、一句任务、留有空白的记录纸。试玩时你不必同时记住十个研究目标，可以把注意力放在对方怎样完成这一回合，以及哪里与你的预想不同。
Plan a playtest around one question

“Try my game and tell me whether it is fun.” A friend sits down, but the invitation still leaves your observation unclear. They might judge the artwork, concentrate on winning, or avoid mentioning confusion to be polite. A small test needs a task that both people understand.
Use the previous chapter’s board to arrange a small test. Watch whether someone new to it can follow the sheet, choose one die, and move the pawn to its destination.
Match the materials to the question

Prepare one consistent version of the 24-space board, two pawns, two ordinary six-sided dice, and the C instructions. To examine this particular relationship, put a pawn on 6 with dice showing 2 and 6. Explain that this is a preset situation. Ask the participant to read, choose a result, and move, without first demonstrating the answer.

A full game from 0 might never produce that combination. Full play can investigate pacing and sustained participation, but cannot guarantee an encounter with the rule relationship under examination. When the scope changes, the task and record should change with it.
Explain how help will work

Try inviting them like this: “Could you help me check whether this sheet is clear? Try one turn using what is written here. Ask if anything is unclear, and stop whenever you like. I’ll note what needs explaining.” Say how you intend to record the session, and ask separately before publishing their words or photographs.

Offer help when it is needed. Note where the person paused, what you said, and what they did afterwards. When you review the record, you can distinguish what the materials explained from what still needed you beside the board.
Leave space for what actually happens

Record version C, starting position 6, results 2 and 6, whether any explanation was given beforehand, and whether the participant has seen this board. Leave blank fields for the actual choice, movement, consulted text, questions, and facilitator prompts. To ask about reasoning after the action, try “How did you decide?” rather than “Did you miss the ladder?”

“How did you choose?” leaves the explanation to the player. “Did you miss the ladder?” has already supplied one. Keep their words beside the movement record. Mark anything you could not capture clearly rather than filling gaps to make the notes look tidy.
Remember that people learn during comparisons

Suppose you compare two ladder drawings. Keep rules and position fixed and change the drawing. If one person sees A and then B, the second attempt may be easier because they already know the answer. With several willing participants, you can alternate which drawing comes first. With very few, at least retain the order in the record instead of claiming the learning effect has disappeared.

Check what is on the table: one version of the materials, one task, and a recording sheet with space to write. During the test, you can watch how the person completes this turn and where it differs from your expectations, without trying to remember ten research goals.
一次顺利移动，能证明什么？
设想记录纸上有这样两次操作。第一次，玩家从第 6 格选了骰子上的 6，走到 12，随后问：“刚才经过 8，是不是该爬梯？”你解释只有停在梯底才爬。第二次摆出同一局面，他选 2，走到 8，再沿梯子到 17。
两次都移到了正确位置，但中间多了你的解释。如果只写“玩家已经理解梯子”，下次修规则时，很容易忘记这份理解是怎样来的。
先找出值得追问的那一句
在选择版 C 里，选 6 是合法动作。值得检查的是后面那句“经过 8，是不是该爬梯”。它让我们知道，玩家还不确定梯子什么时候触发。
原因可能藏在几个地方：规则只写“遇到梯子往上爬”，没有说清落点；图上的梯底不明显；玩家记得另一种玩法。把这些想法放在记录旁边，再回到材料里找。原话和移动轨迹保留下来，后面更换解释时就有东西可查。
你的提示也是这次测试的一部分
第二次走到 17，可以记成“听过解释后，完成了这一局面”。这条记录很有用：说明这个解释至少给了他继续操作的办法。接下来，可以试着把你刚才说的那句话写进规则卡。
要检查卡片能不能独立说明白，就需要请没听过解释的人接手。原来的玩家再做十次，会越来越熟练，却无法重新变成第一次看见材料的人。重复尝试可以观察学习，新的接手者则能检查初次阅读。
一个人指出的遗漏也值得修。如果纸上确实没写“选一颗”，直接补上这句话即可。修完再请人试，才能知道它在实际操作中够不够清楚。
两局长短不同，先回看过程
同样的规则，一局可能连续上梯子，另一局却总在蛇头附近打转。看到时长差别，先核对双方玩的版本、棋盘、先手和收到的帮助，再顺着骰子与选择回看。这样更容易找到差别从哪里开始。
你也可以重放某段骰子序列，检查同样的动作是否会得到同样结果。这适合重现一个问题；若要估计平常一局多长，还得保留自然掷骰的完整对局。
计时也要写起止位置。是从讲解开始，还是第一颗骰子落桌开始？暂停是否算入？没计时就记“未计时”。“感觉挺久”仍然可以保留为玩家原话，只需与钟表记录分开放。
给下一稿留下能用的结论
回到开头，下一步可以很具体：“检查梯底提示，在规则卡上补清落点才触发；找一位没听过讲解的人再试。”这比给整款游戏打一个“易懂”或“难懂”的标签更能帮助动手。
等新记录回来，再看同一句疑问是否仍然出现。如果问题转移到了数格，你也能沿着动作继续查。每一次记录都接着上一次的疑问走，试玩才会慢慢帮你把材料改好。
What does one successful move tell us?

Imagine two attempts on a recording sheet. First, a player at space 6 chooses the die showing 6, moves to 12, and asks, “Should I have climbed when I passed 8?” You explain that the pawn must land at the ladder’s base. You set up the same position again. This time, the player chooses 2, moves to 8, and climbs to 17.
Both moves reached the correct position, but your explanation happened between them. A note saying only “the player understands ladders” would lose how that understanding came about.
Find the remark worth following up
Choosing 6 is legal in choice version C. The useful clue is the question about passing 8: the player is still unsure when the ladder takes effect.

Several things might explain it. Perhaps the rule says “climb when you meet a ladder” without naming the landing space. Perhaps the ladder’s base is hard to see. The player might remember a different way of playing. Put these possibilities beside the record and look for clues in the materials. Keeping the original words and movements gives you something to check when your explanation changes.
Your hint belongs in the record

You can describe the second attempt as “completed this position after an explanation.” That is useful: the explanation gave this person a way to continue. Try putting the sentence you spoke onto the rule card.

To check whether the card works on its own, give it to someone who has not heard the explanation. Ten more attempts by the original player may show increasing fluency, but cannot make the materials new to them again. Repetition can show learning; a new reader can test a first encounter.

An omission noticed by one person is still worth fixing. If the sheet never says “choose one,” add the instruction. Then ask someone to try it, so you can see whether the new wording is clear enough in use.
When two games differ in length, revisit the turns

With identical rules, one game can climb several ladders while another keeps hitting snakes. Before interpreting a timing difference, check the versions, boards, starting player, and help given. Then follow the rolls and choices to find where the games diverged.

You can replay a dice sequence to check whether the same actions produce the same result. That is useful for reproducing a problem. To estimate an ordinary game’s length, you also need complete games with naturally rolled results.

Define the timing interval. Does it start with the explanation or the first roll? Are pauses included? If you did not measure, write “not timed.” Keep “it felt long” as the player’s own words, separate from a clock measurement.
Leave the next draft a usable conclusion

Return to the opening record. A next step could be: “Check the ladder base, clarify that only landing activates it, and ask someone who has not heard the explanation to try.” This gives you more to act on than labelling the entire game easy or difficult.

When the next record arrives, look for the same question. If the difficulty has moved to counting spaces, you can follow that step instead. Each test picks up a question from the previous one, gradually helping you improve the materials.
“最后太拖了”，该改哪条规则？
设想有人试玩后说：“我都快到了，还在那里等。”这是一条值得理解的反馈，却没有直接告诉我们该删掉蛇、加一颗骰子，还是换掉精确到达规则。它描述了一种经历，改法需要再找原因。
先把这句话放回基本版 B 的终点附近：一颗骰子，刚好到 24 才赢，超过就不动。我们用这个假设情境，试着从一句抱怨走到一条可改的规则。
把抱怨还原到一个局面
若棋子在 23，只有掷出 1 才能到达。假设公平六面骰，单次自己回合成功概率是 1/6；其他结果都不动。若暂不考虑对手先结束游戏，平均需要六个自己的回合，才会掷出所需的 1。这不是整局平均时长，也不表示第六次一定成功。
同一句“等太久”，也可能出现在对手思考选骰时，或者发生在不清楚规则而反复查阅时。前者涉及轮流结构，后者涉及表达。先问是从哪个位置开始等、发生了什么、当时哪一版，才能避免用终点规则修一个阅读问题。
为不同原因提出不同改法
如果想减少超出不动，可以从 B 单独试“到达或超过 24 即获胜”。在 23 时任何结果都结束自己的比赛，这一点能由规则推演确认。它也拿掉了最后必须出现精确点数的悬念，是否符合目标仍需比较。
另一种提案是把 B 改为 C，允许从两颗骰子选一个。在 23 时，只要两骰至少一颗为 1 就有获胜选项；公平且独立时概率是 11/36，仍不是必胜。它在终点以外也增加了比较任务，不能只看终点变快的可能，就忽略整个游戏多出来的操作。
先改一件看得见效果的事
如果又改终点、又加选骰、又减少蛇，下一次感觉更顺利时，很难判断哪条变化起作用。可以先保留棋盘，从 B 比较精确到达与到达或超过；或者保留精确到达，从 B 比较 C。两次比较回答的问题不同，应分别记录。
时间不多，就先做最贴近问题的一项。另一种办法写在旁边，标清它打算解决哪段等待。这样既不用一次做完所有草稿，也不会下次又从头猜。
回头看看，这还是你想做的那款游戏吗
如果原来的设计愿望是“每个人都有一次能理解的小选择”，仅改终点或许解决等待，却没有触及愿望。若主要面向轻松共同观看随机结果的场合，增加选骰也未必值得。判断要回到第 4 章的具体邀请，而不是以规则越多为进步。
在改稿旁写一句能复现的说明：“从基本版 B 改起，只把终点改为到达或超过即胜；下一次看末尾还会等多久，大家是否还期待最后一掷。”结果栏先留空。朋友再坐下时，你就知道这一局要与哪一局比较。
“The ending drags.” Which rule should change?

Suppose a playtester says, “I was almost there, but I just kept waiting.” This is worth understanding. It does not yet tell us whether to remove snakes, add a die, or replace the exact-finish rule. A comment describes an experience; a revision needs a more specific account of its cause.

Put the comment beside the finish of base version B: one die, exactly 24 to win, no movement on an overshoot. Use this hypothetical situation to work from a complaint towards one rule you could change.
Recover the situation behind the complaint

At 23, only a 1 reaches the finish. Under a fair-die assumption, success on each own turn has probability 1/6; every other result leaves the pawn still. Temporarily ignoring an opponent ending the game first, the expected wait for that 1 is six own turns. This is neither average game length nor a guarantee of success on the sixth attempt.

“Too much waiting” might instead occur while an opponent considers dice, or during repeated consultation of an unclear rule. One concerns turn structure; the other concerns communication. Identify the position, events, and version before trying to repair a reading problem with a new finish condition.
Match proposals to different causes

To reduce stationary overshoots, try a separate change to B: reaching or passing 24 wins. From 23, any result then finishes the player’s race. Rules reasoning establishes that consequence. It also removes the final demand for an exact result; whether that suits the intended experience remains open.

Another proposal changes B to C, allowing a choice between two dice. At 23, at least one 1 offers a winning selection. With fair independent dice, that probability is 11/36, still not certainty. C adds comparison tasks away from the finish too. A possible improvement to the ending should not hide the extra operations elsewhere.
Start with one change you can follow

Changing the finish, adding die selection, and removing snakes together makes a smoother next game difficult to interpret. Keep the board and compare exact finishing with reaching or passing in B; alternatively, keep the exact finish and compare B with C. These are different questions and deserve separate records.

With limited time, make the proposal closest to the problem first. Write the other one beside it, naming the wait it addresses. You can keep the idea without making every draft now or having to reconstruct it later.
Is this still the game you wanted to make?

If the invitation was “a small understandable decision for each player,” changing only the finish may address waiting without serving that intention. In a relaxed setting centered on watching chance unfold together, die selection may not be worth adding. Return to the specific invitation from chapter 4 instead of treating more rules as progress.

Leave a reproducible note beside the draft: “Start from B and change only the finish to reaching or passing. Next time, watch how long the ending takes and whether people still anticipate the final roll.” Leave the results blank. When friends sit down again, you will know which games to compare.
为什么这一版只留下两颗骰子？
桌上已经摆了好几份草稿：基本版 B、选择版 C、重掷版 R、补给版 E、合作版 S。现在要拿一份交给朋友玩，哪些规则放进袋子，哪些留在笔记本里？
我们先装选择版 C：同一张二十四格棋盘，两个人，每回合掷两颗、选一颗、移动一次，其余沿用基本规则。它是准备交出去试玩的草稿。
回到最初想做的那个小决定
我们的暂定方向是让熟悉掷骰移动的人，看见一个小而明确的行动判断。第 6 格掷出 2 和 6，两个结果分别到 17 与 12，能让“看见点数”连接到“检查落点”。C 不需要额外资源，也不用判断是否在移动前花标记，再记住必须接受重掷结果。
这个取舍也留下了要看的问题。有的回合两颗骰子没有差别，有的人可能更喜欢拿起就掷的节奏。试玩时尤其留意，停下来选骰有没有帮助他们关心路线，还是只多等了一会儿。
说明没有留下的规则解决什么
重掷版让人考虑什么时候花掉一次机会，补给版继续研究机会怎样回来，合作版则改变谁和谁一起成功。把它们各自的用途写清，就可以放心留下这一稿真正需要的规则。
《骆驼大赛》用下注把关心赛道的理由从控制自己的棋子转向判断结果。那是另一条丰富的方向，却需要不同的收益结构与信息判断。看到成熟游戏的巧妙做法之后，我们仍要检查它是否服务于眼前的邀请。
装袋前，哪些事能先检查
可以通过规则核对确认：C 从 6 选 2 会到 17；双骰相同仍只移动一次；两骰都让 23 超出时必须留在原地。也可以检查材料是否完整列出了这些条款。
这些可以在交付前自己走一遍。至于朋友是否能独立读懂、操作是否方便、愿不愿意多想这一步，要给试玩留下时间。先后手的影响也需要另查，不能因为两人拿到相同骰子就划掉。
留一句以后能回看的理由
给 C 写一个版本说明：保留两骰择一、四处蛇梯连接、精确到达和轮流行动；不含标记、补给、合作期限或额外回合。记录选择理由是“先检查小选择能否被理解”，下一步是独立开局与局部落点操作。
等反馈回来，把它和这句理由放在一起。如果选骰让人迟疑，却没有让路线更值得关注，就重新考虑。留过清楚的理由，改主意时才知道自己在回应什么，也更容易向一起设计的人解释。
Why keep only the two dice?
Several drafts are on the table: base B, choice C, reroll R, supply E, and cooperation S. You are about to give a friend one game to try. Which rules go in the bag, and which stay in the notebook?

We will pack choice version C first: the same twenty-four-space board, two people, two dice each turn, one selected result, and one move. The base rules otherwise stay the same. This is the draft we are preparing for playtesting.
Return to the small decision you wanted

Our provisional intention is to give people familiar with roll-and-move a small, understandable decision. At space 6 with results 2 and 6, destinations 17 and 12 connect reading the dice to checking the landing. C needs no extra resource and no additional decision about spending a token before moving and then having to accept a new result.

That choice leaves questions to watch. Some rolls offer no difference between the dice, and some people may prefer to pick up a die and move straight away. During play, notice whether the pause to choose makes the route worth studying or simply adds a wait.
Explain what the omitted rules examine

The reroll version asks when to spend another chance. The supply version asks how those chances return. The cooperation version changes who succeeds together. Once their purposes are written down, you can leave this draft with the rules it needs.

Camel Up uses betting to shift attention from controlling a personal pawn to judging race outcomes. It offers a rich direction, but requires different rewards and information judgments. An elegant mechanism in a published game still needs to be assessed against the invitation of our own design.
What can you check before packing?

Rules inspection can establish that choosing 2 from 6 reaches 17 in C, doubles still produce only one move, and two overshooting results from 23 leave the pawn still. We can also check whether the supplied materials actually state these clauses.

You can walk through these details before the handoff. Leave time for friends to show whether they can read the instructions alone, handle the pieces comfortably, and want to spend time choosing. Turn order also needs investigation; identical dice do not settle its effect.
Leave a reason you can return to

Write a C version note: keep two-dice selection, the four transfers, exact finishing, and alternating turns. Exclude tokens, replenishment, a cooperative deadline, and extra turns. Record the reason as “first examine whether the small choice can be understood,” followed by independent setup and a local landing task.

When feedback comes back, put it beside that reason. If choosing creates hesitation without making the route more interesting, reconsider. A written reason helps you see what you are responding to and explain a changed direction to someone designing with you.
把规则交出去，你不在旁边也能开始吗？
你已经看过这张棋盘很多次，第 8 格该去哪儿，一眼就知道。朋友第一次接手时，只有纸上的图和说明。先把这一套材料单独放好，看看它离开你的讲解，还能不能让人开局。
本章给出可以独立使用的 C 版说明。它是一桌点子自编的《二十四格小赛跑》v0.1，两骰择一版，借《蛇梯棋》的移动关系提出设计问题，不代表某个出版版本的规则。
准备一份完整的材料
需要两位玩家、每人一枚能区分的棋子、两颗普通六面骰，以及一张按顺序标有 1 到 24 的棋盘。编号决定相邻关系；可以在纸上排成四行，每行六格，交替方向，或排成另一种清楚的连续路线。在第 1 格之前标一个棋盘外的起点 0。
棋盘仅有四处特殊连接：梯子 3 → 11、8 → 17；蛇 14 → 4、22 → 12。其他格都是普通格。请把方向和两个端点写清。两枚棋子都放在 0，随机决定一位先手，例如抛硬币，然后轮流行动。没有标记、手牌、补给、轮数上限，也不需要掷出 6 才能起步。
每个回合只移动一次
轮到你时，同时掷两颗骰子，选择其中一颗的点数，让自己的棋子按编号增加的方向前进相同步数，另一颗不使用。两骰相同仍只移动一次，不能相加，不能重掷，掷出 6 也没有额外回合。可以先查看两个结果各自会到哪里，再决定。
如果选择的点数会让你超过 24，就留在回合开始的位置，不移动、不触发格子效果，结束回合。即使另一颗能够移动，你也可以选择会超出的那颗。两颗都超出时，同样原地结束回合。
停下来，才检查蛇和梯子
没有超出时，先走完选中的步数。只有最终落在 3、8、14、22，才按对应箭头移动到 11、17、4、12。经过这些格子不触发；落在梯顶或蛇尾也不反向移动。这张棋盘的四个目的地都不是新的触发格，因此一次结算后就结束回合。
例如从 6 选 2：走到 8，再沿梯子到 17。从 6 选 6：经过 8，停在 12，不爬梯。从 20 选 2：落在 22，再沿蛇到 12。两枚棋子可以在同一格，经过对手也没有阻挡、推挤或吃子效果。
到达 24，立即结束
第一个恰好到达 24 的玩家获胜，游戏当即结束，不补完这一轮。因此若你在 20 并选 4，就获胜；在 23 选 2，则超出而不动。由于每次只有一位玩家移动，这个版本不会发生同时到达的平局，不需要另加平局判定。
这份规则使用两骰择一版 C，开局无需加入前面实验中的单骰玩法、重掷标记、补给或合作期限。按以上材料即可准备并开始。
听听他们在哪一步问你
观察摆棋、第一回合和第一次遇到特殊格。对方需要帮助时就解释，同时记下发生在哪一步。如果他们相加骰子，问问是从哪句说明这样理解的；那句话通常比“读者看错”更能帮助修订。
回看问题时，先查纸上有没有写、写法是否有两种读法，再问对方是否喜欢这个玩法。补上遗漏、消除歧义、改变设计，分别需要不同的动作。把他们真正拿在手里的说明改好，再请下一位接手。
Can someone start without you beside them?

You have seen this board so often that you know where space 8 leads at a glance. A friend receives only the drawing and instructions. Put those materials together on their own and see whether they can get a game started without your explanation.

Here are self-contained instructions for The 24-Space Race v0.1, choice version C. It is an original teaching game from Make Games with Sichuang using movement relationships familiar from Snakes and Ladders, not the rules of a particular published edition.
Prepare a complete set of materials

You need two players, one distinguishable pawn each, two ordinary six-sided dice, and a board numbered consecutively from 1 to 24. Numbers determine adjacency. You can arrange four rows of six in alternating directions, or draw another clearly ordered route. Mark start 0 outside the board before space 1.

There are exactly four special connections: ladders 3 → 11 and 8 → 17; snakes 14 → 4 and 22 → 12. All other spaces are ordinary. Mark both endpoints and directions clearly. Put both pawns at 0 and choose a first player randomly, for example by a coin toss, then alternate turns. There are no tokens, cards, supplies, or round limit. You do not need to roll a 6 to start.
Make one move on your turn

Roll both dice together. Choose the value on one die and advance your pawn that many spaces in increasing number order. Ignore the other die. Doubles still give only one move. Do not add the values, reroll, or take an extra turn for a 6. You may examine both destinations before choosing.

If your selected result would take you beyond 24, stay where you began the turn. Do not move or activate any space; end the turn. You may choose an overshooting result even if the other die allows movement. If both results overshoot, stay and end the turn.
Check transfers only after landing

Without an overshoot, complete the selected number of steps first. Landing on 3, 8, 14, or 22 then transfers the pawn to 11, 17, 4, or 12 respectively. Passing these spaces does nothing. Landing at a ladder top or snake tail does not transfer backward. None of this board’s four destinations is another trigger, so resolution then ends the turn.

For example, from 6 choose 2: reach 8 and climb to 17. From 6 choose 6: pass 8 and end at 12 without climbing. From 20 choose 2: reach 22 and slide to 12. Both pawns may occupy one space. Passing or landing on another pawn never blocks, pushes, or captures it.
Reach 24 and end immediately

The first player to reach exactly 24 wins, ending the game immediately without completing the round. From 20, choosing 4 wins. From 23, choosing 2 overshoots and leaves you still. Only one player moves at a time, so simultaneous arrival and its associated tie do not occur in this version.

These instructions use choice version C. Setup needs no single-die procedure, reroll tokens, supply rule, or cooperation deadline from the earlier experiments. Use the materials above to prepare and begin.
Listen for the step where they ask for help

Watch setup, the first turn, and the first special space. Explain when someone needs help, and note where it happened. If they add the dice, ask which wording led them to do that. The sentence they point to is usually more useful for revision than a note saying “reader error.”

When reviewing a question, first check whether the rule is present and whether its wording allows two readings. Then ask whether the person likes the rule itself. Filling a gap, clarifying a sentence, and changing the design require different work. Revise the sheet they actually received before the next handoff.
把这一版装好，交给下一位玩家
一位朋友只收到棋盘图片，另一位收到重掷标记说明，两人却以为在讨论同一版。即使你脑中已经选定 C，他们桌上的游戏仍然可能不同。分享之前，需要把规则、材料与版本放在一起。
这次准备分享《二十四格小赛跑》C v0.1：两人、两骰择一、二十四格、四处蛇梯连接、刚好到终点。上一章的完整规则可以直接使用，现在把它和棋盘放在一起，写一段朋友收到后看得懂的邀请。
让材料指向同一局
一套最小材料包括棋盘、完整规则，以及两枚棋子和两颗普通六面骰的准备说明。纸片可以代替棋子，只要能分辨谁是谁。棋盘要同时标明 0 和 24、3 → 11、8 → 17、14 → 4、22 → 12，并能辨认编号顺序。
在规则和棋盘上都写 C v0.1。材料包不包含重掷标记、补给提示或十轮合作期限。若想展示研究经过，可以另附版本比较表，明确 B、R、E、S 是其他实验，不能把这些提示混在实际开局页里。接手者不应靠读完整门课程来猜哪些规则仍然有效。
写一段朋友能接着做的邀请
可以写：“我做了一个两人纸上赛跑，还没找人试过。你能按这张说明自己开局吗？如果哪一步不清楚，帮我圈出来；也请记一下有没有问别人。玩过之后，我想听听你觉得选骰这一步怎么样。”
若只准备了局部测试，就明确从第 6 格与预设点数开始，不声称测了整局节奏。若邀请完整游玩，可以记录开局到结束的时间和回合，但应说明计时范围。是否愿意再次玩，也可以直接询问，不必从笑声推断长期兴趣。
在版本号旁写清改了什么
交出去前，自己核对一次关键移动：从 6 选 2 到 17，从 20 选 2 到 12，从 23 选 2 原地不动。邀请里则留下自己还想知道的事，例如是否能独立开局、等候是否太长。接手者就知道哪些地方最值得反馈。
假设后续只改清“经过不触发”的措辞，可以记为 C v0.2 的表达修订，注明棋盘与玩法未改；如果改成到达或超过终点，则是玩法修订，需要列出新的结束条件。不要只写“优化体验”，让后来的人无法复现差异。
留好草稿，还可以继续走
想继续研究共同资源和分工，可以切换到完整的过河路线。那里的一次收集，会改变同伴之后能不能前进；在这里，一个骰子选择改变的是自己在比赛中的位置。两张棋盘会带你看见不同的设计问题。
从最初那次滑下蛇，到现在能交出去的一套材料，你已经有了可以继续修改的东西。先找两个人坐下，照这份规则开始。下一稿最有用的线索，可能就在他们拿起骰子、停下来问一句的那一刻。
Pack this version for the next player

One friend receives a board image; another receives instructions for reroll tokens. Both think they are discussing the same version. Even if you have chosen C in your own mind, the games on their tables may differ. Before sharing, bring rules, materials, and version together.

We are sharing The 24-Space Race C v0.1: two players, a choice between two dice, twenty-four spaces, four transfers, and an exact finish. The previous chapter’s complete rules are ready to use. Put them with the board and write an invitation your friend can act on.
Make every component point to the same game

A minimal set contains the board, full instructions, and a list asking for two pawns and two ordinary six-sided dice. Distinguishable paper pieces can replace pawns. The board should show 0 and 24, transfers 3 → 11, 8 → 17, 14 → 4, and 22 → 12, and an understandable number order.

Mark both rules and board C v0.1. Exclude reroll tokens, replenishment reminders, and the ten-round cooperative deadline. If you want to show the investigation, put B, R, E, and S in a separate comparison sheet identified as other experiments. Recipients should not need the whole course to guess which rules apply to their setup.
Write an invitation someone can use

Try this: “I’ve made a two-player paper race and haven’t playtested it yet. Could you try setting up from this sheet? Circle any step that is unclear and note whether you asked someone for help. Afterwards, I’d like to hear what you thought of choosing a die.”

For a local test, state that it begins at space 6 with preset dice, and do not claim to investigate full-game pacing. For complete play, you can record turns and elapsed time, defining when timing starts and stops. You can also ask whether someone wants another game instead of inferring lasting interest from laughter.
Put the change beside the version number

Before sending it, check the key moves yourself: choosing 2 from 6 reaches 17; choosing 2 from 20 reaches 12; choosing 2 from 23 leaves the pawn still. In the invitation, name what you still want to learn, such as whether setup works without help or the waits feel too long. Recipients then know where feedback would be useful.

Suppose a later revision only clarifies that passing does not activate a space. You might label it C v0.2, noting a communication change without changing the board or play. Replacing exact finishing with reaching or passing is a rules change and needs a new ending clause. “Improved the experience” alone does not let someone reproduce the difference.
Keep the drafts—you can take them further

To keep exploring shared resources and divided work, switch to the complete river path. There, collecting a plank can change whether your partner can advance. Here, choosing a die changes your own position in the race. The two boards give you different design questions to follow.

From that first slide down a snake to this set of materials, you have made something you can keep revising. Find two people, set out the board, and start with these rules. A useful clue for the next draft may arrive when someone picks up the dice and pauses to ask a question.
一局游戏，是怎样一步步发生的？
小林把一只小兔棋子放在纸上，小雨把小刺猬放在它旁边。两只动物面前是一条河。小林伸手想把小兔直接放到对岸，小雨却说：“先等等，它能一下子跳过去吗？”
这就是我们开始理解游戏的地方。纸上的动物可以被手拿到任何地方，但这一局允许怎样移动，需要大家先说好。接下来，我们跟着一个为讲解编写的小例子，看他们怎样开始、怎样继续，又在什么时候停下。你只需跟着文字读，不用准备棋子。
先知道要去哪里
这条河只有一条路线：起点岸，第一块踏脚石，第二块踏脚石，最后是对岸。两只动物都从起点出发，只能向前走到相邻的位置，不能跳格，也不能退回去。它们可以站在同一块石头上，不会挡住彼此。
小林负责小兔，小雨负责小刺猬。他们想让两只动物都到对岸，一只先到了还不算成功。桌子中央放着四块木板，两人共用；谁移动，都从这里取。每向前走一步就要用掉一块木板，表示临时搭桥。用过的木板放到一旁，这一局不能再拿回来使用。桌外另放十六块备用纸片，代表还没收集到的新木板；它们还不属于中央的可用木板。
现在，纸上的几样东西有了联系。小兔想前进，需要中央还有木板；小兔用掉一块，小刺猬接下来可用的就少了一块。只认识动物和木板的名称，还不够解释这局怎样玩。我们还要知道，一样东西的变化会怎样影响另一样东西。
轮到你，先做一件事
小林先行动，然后小雨行动。两人各行动一次，才算完成一轮；整局最多四轮。轮到一个人做事的这段机会，叫作他的“回合”。所以，一轮里有小林和小雨两个回合。
每个回合只能做一件事。你可以花一块木板，让自己的动物向前走一步。如果动物还在起点岸，也可以留在原地，从桌外的备用纸片中收集两块新木板，放进中央。你还可以等待，这次不移动，也不增加木板。木板不够时不能前进，离开起点后也不能再收集。
小雨若选择收集，不能紧接着又走一步；那要等下次轮到她。小兔到了对岸以后就留在那里，之后轮到小林时只能等待。两人可以商量，但各自决定自己动物的行动。
这些规定把一次动作的起点和终点说清了。我们知道谁能做、可以选什么、做完会改变什么，也知道什么时候该交给下一个人。
跟着两只动物走完四轮
第一轮，小林用一块木板，小兔走上第一块石头。中央从四块变成三块。小雨让小刺猬留在岸边，收集两块，中央便有五块。第一轮结束时，小兔走在前面，小刺猬还没出发，但两人可用的木板比刚才多了。
第二轮，两人都选择前进。小兔来到第二块石头，小刺猬来到第一块；各用掉一块，中央剩三块。
第三轮，小兔再用一块，抵达对岸。小刺猬也向前一步，来到第二块石头，中央还剩一块。小兔已经安全了，不过两人的目标还没完成：小刺猬也得过去。
第四轮，轮到小林，他让已经到岸的小兔等待。随后小雨用掉最后一块木板，小刺猬也抵达对岸。两只都到了，这局立刻结束，两人共同获胜。假如第四轮结束时还有一只没到，他们就会失败。
这里既有“什么时候停”，也有“怎样算成功”。只有小兔到了，不能提前宣布大家赢了；木板花光，也不一定失败——刚才最后一块恰好把最后一只动物送到了岸上。
下一步，取决于现在的局面
再看第一轮结束的那一刻：小兔在第一块石头，小刺猬在起点，中央有五块木板，已经过了一轮。这些会影响后续行动的信息，可以合起来叫“当前局面”，也可以简称为游戏的“状态”。
它不只是一个分数。小刺猬还在起点，意味着它仍能收集；小兔已经离岸，意味着它失去了这项做法。五块木板意味着接下来最多还能支付五次前进。已经用掉一轮，意味着每只动物最多还剩三次行动机会。
于是，游戏一边进行，下一步能做什么也一边改变。规则把这些变化接在一起；玩家再根据新的局面决定怎么做。设计者写下的不是一串必须照演的台词，而是大家据以行动的共同约定。
刚才我们走完的是一种成功办法。小雨第一轮为什么没有跟着小兔一起走？两个人都前进，看起来不是更快吗？这是一个值得留下的问题。接下来先学会怎样观察：我们确实看见了哪些动作，又给这些动作加上了什么解释。之后再回到这次选择，细看它怎样改变后面的路。
这是一款为讲解设计而编写的小草稿。你已经能照着规则，让两只动物走过河；接着就可以请朋友试，看看他们在哪一步讨论、哪里停下来，又会不会想再玩。
How Does a Game Happen, One Move at a Time?

Lin places a Rabbit piece on a sheet of paper. Yu puts Hedgehog beside it. A river lies ahead. Lin reaches to put Rabbit straight on the far bank, but Yu stops him: “Wait—can it jump all the way across?”

This is a useful place to begin understanding games. A hand can put a piece anywhere. What the piece may do in this game depends on the rules everyone agrees to use. We will follow an invented example from its beginning to its end. You can follow it in the text; you do not need any pieces.
Know Where You Are Going

There is one route across the river: the starting bank, the first stepping stone, the second stepping stone, and the far bank. Both animals start on the starting bank. They can move only to the next position ahead, without skipping a position or going backward. They may share any position, so neither blocks the other.

Lin controls Rabbit and Yu controls Hedgehog. Their goal is to get both animals across. Getting just one across is not enough. Four planks lie in the middle of the table for them to share. Each step forward uses one plank to make a temporary bridge. Used planks are put aside and cannot be used again during this game. Another sixteen paper pieces sit outside the playing area as spare planks that have not yet been collected. They are not part of the available shared supply.

The objects now connect to one another. Rabbit needs a plank to move. When Rabbit uses one, Hedgehog has one fewer available. Knowing the names of the animals and the planks would not explain how this game works. We need to follow how a change to one affects the others.
On Your Turn, Do One Thing
Lin acts first, then Yu. Each person's opportunity to act is a turn. When both have taken a turn, one round is complete. The game lasts at most four rounds.

On a turn, you choose one thing to do. You may spend one shared plank to move your animal one position forward. If it is still on the starting bank, you may instead keep it there and collect two new planks from those spare pieces and add them to the shared supply. You may also wait, without moving or collecting anything. You cannot move without enough planks, and you cannot collect after leaving the starting bank.

If Yu collects, she cannot move immediately afterward; she must wait for her next turn. An animal that reaches the far bank stays there. Its player can only wait on later turns. The players may discuss their plans, but each decides their own animal's action.
These rules give an action a clear beginning and end. We know who can act, what they may choose, what changes afterward, and when the next person gets a turn.
Follow Both Animals Through Four Rounds

In the first round, Lin spends one plank and moves Rabbit onto the first stone. Three planks remain. Yu keeps Hedgehog on the starting bank and collects two, bringing the shared supply to five. Rabbit is ahead and Hedgehog has not left, but they now have more planks available.
In the second round, both move. Rabbit reaches the second stone; Hedgehog reaches the first. They each spend a plank, leaving three.

In the third round, Rabbit spends a plank to reach the far bank. Hedgehog also moves forward, reaching the second stone. One plank remains. Rabbit is safe, but their shared goal is still unfinished: Hedgehog must cross too.

In the fourth round, Lin waits with Rabbit on the far bank. Yu then spends the last plank to bring Hedgehog across. Both animals have arrived, so the game ends immediately with a shared win. If either animal had still been short of the far bank at the end of the fourth round, they would have lost.

The rules tell us both when to stop and what counts as success. Rabbit arriving alone does not mean they have won. Using the last plank does not necessarily mean failure, either: here, it took the last animal to the far bank.
What Comes Next Depends on What Is Here Now

Return to the end of the first round. Rabbit is on the first stone. Hedgehog is on the starting bank. Five planks remain, and one round has passed. Together, the information that matters to what can happen next forms the current situation, often called the game's state.

It includes more than a score. Hedgehog's position means it can still collect. Rabbit's position means it no longer can. Five planks can pay for five more forward moves. With one round used, each animal has at most three turns left.

As the game proceeds, what is possible next changes too. Rules connect these changes, and players decide what to do in the new situation. The designer has written a shared agreement for acting, rather than a script that everyone must perform word for word.

We have followed one way to succeed. Why did Yu stay behind in the first round? Wouldn't moving both animals forward have been faster? Keep that question. First, we will learn how to observe: which actions did we actually see, and what explanations have we added to them? Later we will return to this choice and examine how it changes the road ahead.

This little draft was written to explain design. You can now follow its rules and get both animals across. Ask friends to try it, and watch where they discuss a move, where they pause, and whether they want another game.
看过一局以后，究竟看到了什么？
第一轮，小林让小兔前进一步，中央木板从四块变成三块。轮到小雨，她让小刺猬留在起点，收集两块新木板，中央于是有了五块。一只动物走远了，另一只没有动。只看位置，很容易觉得小林在推进游戏，小雨在拖延。
可是，留下收集也改变了局面。两只动物总共要走六步，最初的四块木板不够。如果双方第一轮都前进，剩下的两块就无法支持后面的四步，而它们已经离开了唯一能收集的起点。位置和木板一起看，才看得出“没有移动”也可能帮助过河。
设计者观察游戏，首先要练习把这样的变化看完整。否则，很可能把“动物没动”误当成“这一回合没有作用”，接着增加一个根本不需要的新动作。
先把眼前发生的事说准
一句“他们合作得很好”已经包含了判断。相比之下，“小林移动后，中央剩三块；小雨选择收集，中央变成五块”让别人也能重建这个局面。接着可以记下当时说了什么、先做了什么、随后发生了什么。先后顺序很有用：小雨是在小林提醒后收集，还是自己先提出留下？这两种过程可能得到同样的木板数量，却给设计者留下不同的问题。
这里的先后差别只是两种假设，并不是已经发生的试玩。想象第一种过程，小林说“你别走，先拿木板”，小雨照做。我们能说他提出了安排，她采用了它；仅凭这句话，还不能说她没有想法，也不能说她喜欢被提醒。她也许早有同样的计划，也许正在学习动作。
在纸上画一个小箭头，标出木板从四到三再到五，比急着给人贴“会合作”或“不主动”的标签更有用。箭头留下的是可以核对的变化，标签却容易掩盖我们还不知道的部分。
我的感受，也是一条有范围的线索
假如你亲自玩这一局，等小雨决定时觉得着急，这个感受可以留下。还可以补上具体时刻：小兔已经在第一块踏脚石上，中央剩三块，你担心下一轮没有木板。这样，“着急”就和一个局面连在一起了。
但你的着急不能代替小雨的感受。她可能觉得终于看懂了计划，正在兴奋地计算；也可能因为不知道收集会不会结束回合而犹豫。同样的停顿，可能来自认真比较，也可能来自规则疑问。观察到她停下来，与知道她为什么停下来，是两步不同的工作。
可以问“刚才轮到你时，你在考虑什么？”再把她的回答和动作放在一起看。若抢先问“是不是规则太难了？”，问题里已经塞进了设计者的猜测。她即使同意，也未必说明这就是最初的原因。
从一件小事，得到下一步问题
观察不必把桌上的每句话都抄下来。想看两人怎样决定谁留下，就留意提出计划、回应计划和实际行动的时点；想看木板是否容易分清，就留意纸片被拿起、放下和询问的地方。关注点帮我们选择要留下什么，却不能让不合预期的事情消失。如果两人根本没看懂轮到谁，这件事会影响之后的合作，也应该记住。
这一轮之后，比较稳妥的问题是：“玩家能否看出，留在起点也会帮助共同目标？”直接得出“应该让收集也前进一步”，则过早跳到了改法。这个改法还会取消留下来的代价，改变整个过河安排。
把动作、自己的感受和猜想分别写下，再回看一次。你会更容易找到还不知道的地方，也知道下一次该看谁、该问哪一句。
What Have You Actually Seen After Watching a Game?

In the first round, Lin moves Rabbit forward one step. The shared supply drops from four planks to three. Yu then keeps Hedgehog on the starting bank and collects two new planks, bringing the supply to five. One animal has moved ahead; the other has stayed still. If we watch positions alone, Lin seems to be making progress while Yu holds things up.

But collecting changes the situation too. The animals need six moves between them, and their starting four planks cannot pay for all six. If both move in the first round, the two remaining planks cannot cover the four moves still needed. Both animals have also left the only place where they can collect. Watching positions and planks together reveals how staying still can help them cross.
A designer needs to notice the whole change. Otherwise, “the animal did not move” can become “that turn did nothing,” followed by a new action the game never needed.
Describe what happened before judging it

“They worked well together” already includes a judgment. “After Lin moved, three planks remained; Yu collected, bringing the supply to five” lets someone else reconstruct the situation. We can then add what people said, what they did first, and what happened next. Order matters: did Yu collect after a reminder from Lin, or did she suggest staying behind? Both paths can produce five planks while raising different questions.

These are two imagined possibilities, not reports of a real playtest. Suppose Lin says, “Stay there and collect first,” and Yu does. We can say that he proposed a plan and she followed it. That sentence alone cannot tell us whether she had ideas of her own or enjoyed the reminder. She may already have had the same plan, or she may still be learning the actions.

A little arrow showing the supply changing from four to three to five is more useful than quickly calling someone “cooperative” or “passive.” The arrow preserves a change we can check. The label can hide what we still do not know.
Your feelings are clues with limits

If you play this round and feel impatient while Yu decides, you can keep that observation too. Add the moment: Rabbit was on the first stepping stone, three planks remained, and you were worried about having enough next round. Now the feeling is connected to a particular situation.

Your impatience cannot tell us how Yu felt. She might be excited because she has just understood the plan. Or she might be unsure whether collecting ends her turn. The same pause could come from comparing choices or from a question about the rules. Seeing her pause and knowing why she paused are separate steps.

You could ask, “What were you considering when it was your turn?” and compare her answer with her actions. Asking “Were the rules too difficult?” puts the designer’s guess inside the question. Even if she agrees, that may not have been the original cause.
Turn a small event into a useful question

Observing does not require writing down every word. To understand how players decide who stays behind, watch when they propose plans, respond, and act. To understand whether the planks are easy to distinguish, watch where pieces are picked up and placed, and where questions arise. A focus helps us choose what to record. It should still leave room for surprises. If neither player knows whose turn it is, that will affect their cooperation too.

After this round, a useful question is: “Can players recognize that staying on the starting bank can help their shared goal?” Jumping straight to “collecting should also move the animal forward” skips ahead to a change. That change would remove the cost of staying behind and alter how the crossing works.
Write the actions, your own feelings, and your guesses separately, then read them back. The gaps become easier to find, along with who to watch and what to ask next time.
这款游戏给谁，在什么时候玩？
设想小林把小动物过河带到活动室。小雨愿意一起看看，但十分钟后要去上课。两人身边只有一张小桌子，桌上还放着书包。这和周末有整张桌子、可以慢慢商量的下午，是两种不同的开始。
同一套规则没有改变，能用来听说明、摆材料和考虑下一步的条件却变了。设计游戏时，“给新手玩”还不够具体。我们需要知道，新手将在什么情况下遇见它。
年龄没有替我们回答的问题
同样十二岁的两个人，一个可能已经熟悉轮流行动，另一个第一次听见“每人一次才算一轮”。前者未必喜欢竞争，后者也未必只想玩简单的游戏。年龄可以提醒我们检查用词，却不能替代这些具体了解。
回到这次假设的活动室相遇，小林可以先说：“这是两个人一起想办法过河的游戏。你愿意看一轮，再决定要不要接着玩吗？”小雨知道自己将做什么，也知道现在的答应没有包下整个下午。若她只想观看，小林可以演示两只动物的一轮，不把旁观误算成她已加入游戏。
介绍还可以消除一种不必要的疑惑。假如小雨问：“小兔先到了，是我输了吗？”答案是，两只都到岸才一起获胜，没有个人名次。这个问题暴露的是她带来的理解方式。把目标说清，比从这个问题判断她“不会玩”更有用。
时间要装下游戏之外的事
基本版最多四轮，但四轮不是四分钟。第一次读动作、数木板、商量谁留在起点收集，都需要时间；玩完还要收拾。没有实际计时，就不能向小雨保证十分钟一定够。
有几种不同的处理办法。今天只演示第一轮，目标是看懂一次行动；两人另约一段更充裕的时间，目标是完成一局；或者先尝试完整游戏，到了上课时间就停下。前两种改变这次活动的安排，第三种需要事先知道如何停。
如果铃声响了而两只动物还没到岸，可以把这次记录为“中途停止”，然后收好材料。基本规则的失败发生在第四轮结束仍未到齐；上课打断不是动物又做了一个动作，也不用把自愿参与变成必须熬完的承诺。
桌面同样要具体看。两只动物、一条路线、中央可用木板、旁边已用木板以及桌外备用纸片，需要各自找得到的地方。桌子太挤，可以先挪开书包或换位置。是否看得清、够得着，后面还会仔细讨论；现在先发现游戏依赖哪些条件。
让人谈什么，比让人说多少更重要
假如这次见面的愿望是两人一起商量，值得保留的可能是：“谁这次留在起点，好让另一只先走？”若他们一边聊天一边玩，每一步又要读一长段新文字，规则阅读就会和聊天争用注意。多加故事或选择，未必更符合这次见面的愿望。
另一桌的人可能恰好想安静计算。有明确的路线和有限木板，就有东西可想。小林不能因为对方话少，便认定需要增加抢答；也不能因为一个人很兴奋，就认定另一个人同样享受。这些判断需要当事人的话和具体发生的事来修正。
起点是可以改的判断
现在我们能给这次设计一个比“适合十二岁”更清楚的起点：“两位第一次接触它的朋友，在能坐下摆材料的地方，愿意用一段不赶时间的空闲，共同商量一个短小问题。”这里的每一项都有用处：两人限制人数，初次接触要求说明够清楚，共同商量给动作之间的关系一个方向。
这些条件可以随着了解改变。若朋友总是错开时间，可能要设计能保存局面和轮次的另一种玩法；若大家其实只想看一段演示，也可以把这次活动做成可停下观看的介绍。条件变了，设计方向可以跟着改，无须先责怪玩家没照原计划出现。
把这次邀请的地点、时间和参与者写在草稿旁边。准备新规则时，回来看一眼：这里坐得下吗，来得及试吗，对方有没有机会做自己想做的事？
Who Will Play This Game, and When?

Imagine Lin bringing the animal crossing game to an activity room. Yu would like to see it, but she has a class in ten minutes. They have a small table with schoolbags already on it. This is a different starting point from a weekend afternoon with a whole table and time to talk.

The rules are the same. The conditions for hearing an explanation, setting out pieces, and considering a move have changed. “For beginners” is not yet specific enough for a design. We need to know how those beginners will encounter it.
Questions an age cannot answer

Two twelve-year-olds may bring different experience. One already understands taking turns; the other first encounters the idea that both players must act to complete a round. The experienced player may dislike competition, while the newcomer may want a substantial challenge. Age can prompt us to check our wording. It cannot answer these more specific questions.

In our imagined meeting, Lin could say, “This is a game about finding a way across together. Would you like to see one round, then decide whether to continue?” Yu can understand both the activity and the extent of her agreement. If she prefers to watch, Lin can demonstrate a round for both animals without treating her presence as a commitment to play.

An introduction can also resolve an unnecessary uncertainty. Suppose Yu asks, “If Rabbit arrives first, have I lost?” Both animals must arrive for a shared win; there are no individual places. Her question reveals an expectation she brought with her. Explaining the goal is more useful than deciding that she is bad at games.
Time must hold more than the turns

The basic game lasts at most four rounds, but four rounds do not mean four minutes. Reading the actions, counting planks, and discussing who will stay at the start to collect all take time. Packing up does too. Without timing an actual session, we cannot promise that ten minutes will be enough.

Different arrangements serve different purposes. Today they could demonstrate just the first round to understand an action. They could arrange more time to finish a game. Or they could attempt a whole game and stop when class begins. The first two change the plan for this meeting. The third needs an understood way to stop.

If the bell rings before both animals arrive, they can record the session as “stopped partway” and pack up. Under the basic rules, a loss occurs when the fourth round ends without both animals across. A class interrupting the session is not another animal action, and agreeing to try a game need not become an obligation to finish it.

Space also needs a concrete look. The animals, route, available planks in the center, used planks beside them, and reserve paper pieces off the table need identifiable places. Moving the bags or changing tables may help. Later we will examine seeing and reaching the pieces more closely. For now, we are noticing conditions the game depends on.
What people discuss matters more than how much they speak

Suppose the purpose of this meeting is to think together. A question worth preserving might be, “Who stays at the start this time so the other animal can move?” If they want to chat while playing, a long new passage to read on every turn would compete with that conversation. More story or more choices may not serve this particular meeting.

Another pair may want quiet calculation. A clear route and a limited supply of planks give them something to consider. Quiet players do not automatically need a speed contest added, and one person’s excitement does not establish the other person’s enjoyment. Their accounts and specific events can help revise our assumptions.
A starting judgment can change

We can now describe a more useful starting point than “suitable for twelve-year-olds”: “Two friends meeting this game for the first time, somewhere they can sit and lay out pieces, with an unhurried stretch of free time to discuss a small shared problem.” Each part does work. Two people sets a player count. First contact calls for a clear explanation. Shared discussion gives a direction to the relationships between actions.

These conditions can change as we learn. If the friends can never arrive together, a different design might preserve the position and turns between visits. If people mainly want to watch a demonstration, the meeting could become an introduction they can leave when they wish. A changed situation can justify a changed direction without blaming people for failing to appear as expected.
Keep the place, time, and participants beside the draft. When preparing a new rule, check back: will it fit this table and this meeting, and give the people invited something they want to do?
还没有规则时，先确定什么？
“我们来做一个小动物过河游戏。”听起来已经有了方向，两位设计者却可能在想完全不同的事。一位想让动物争着先到岸，另一位想让它们一起想办法。河、木板和可爱的角色可以完全相同，玩家要关心的事却不同。
先把这处分歧说清，比马上决定木板画多大更有帮助。争先过河时，阻碍对方也许很有用；共同过河时，让同伴留下准备材料也许是在帮助整个队伍。目的没有说清，之后每增加一条规则，都可能把游戏拉向不同方向。
先描述想让人遇到的处境
我们已经见过完整的过河基本版。现在试着倒过来，想象规则尚未确定时，怎样为它写一个暂定方向：两个人坐在一张小桌边，玩一局能在短暂空闲里结束的纸片游戏。他们需要商量各自什么时候前进、什么时候为共同目标做准备；希望每个人都有自己的决定，而双方都到岸才算完成。
这几句话可以成为一份很短的设计简报。它说明为谁、在什么条件下做、希望发生什么，也留下尚未确定的地方。此时不必知道一定用四轮、四块木板，或一定收集两块。那些是之后可以比较的规则方案。
“希望两人商量”也还不是已经实现的结果。一人可能想好全部安排，另一人只照做。所以还可以留下一个要观察的问题：两个人是否都有机会提出和选择自己的行动？写下目标，是为了让后来的草稿有一个可检查的方向。
哪些事情固定，哪些事情还能换？
假设这次只能使用纸和笔，桌面也不大，这是制作条件。它会让长长的立体河道不太合适，却不自动决定玩家应当合作还是竞争。“双方都到岸才算完成”则是当前选择的体验方向。为了实现它，可以尝试共用木板，也可以先构思别的互相帮助方式。
把条件和方向分开，我们就知道该怎样回应新点子。“加一个会发光的电子桥”可能超出这次能做的材料；“第一个到岸的人单独获胜”则改变了谁在乎谁能过河。两者都不是单纯的好坏问题，而是在改变简报中的不同部分。
有些限制只是为了先做出一小段可玩的东西。我们可以暂时只画一条路线，先看两人怎样分配准备与前进。等这个关系清楚后，再判断第二条路线是否有帮助。暂时没做，不等于永远禁止。
简报怎样帮助选择，又不把人困住？
假如桌上有两个候选点子：让动物换三种帽子，或者让留在起点的动物为双方取得木板。前者也许有趣，但在目前的方向下，后者更直接地让“一人的准备影响两人的行程”出现。这个理由足够让我们先试收集，不需要宣布帽子永远没有价值。
简报也可能需要改变。如果之后发现自己更想做轻松的角色装扮游戏，就可以承认方向变了，再重新考虑规则。问题在于改了方向却还用旧目标评价每个点子：一边要求紧张规划，一边不断消除所有需要规划的限制，改稿便会互相抵消。
现在，“做个好玩的游戏”已经变成两个人可以讨论的方向。拿着这张简报挑一个办法，先写出能摆到桌上的动作；试玩以后，还可以带着具体发现回来改这几句话。
What Can You Decide Before You Have Rules?

“Let’s make a game about animals crossing a river.” That sounds like a direction, yet two designers may picture very different games. One imagines animals racing to arrive first. The other imagines them working things out together. The river, planks, and cute characters could look identical while giving players different things to care about.

Clearing up that difference helps more than immediately deciding how large to draw a plank. In a race, getting in someone’s way might be useful. In a shared crossing, staying behind to prepare materials might help the whole team. Without a clear purpose, each added rule could pull the game in a different direction.
Describe the situation you want players to face

We have already seen the complete base crossing game. Now imagine working backward to a time when its rules were undecided. A provisional direction might be: two people at a small table play a paper game that fits into a short break. They discuss when each should move and when someone should prepare for their shared goal. Each person should have decisions of their own, and the task is complete only when both animals arrive.

Those few sentences can serve as a short design brief. They say who the game is for, the conditions it must fit, and what we hope will happen. They also leave things open. We do not yet need to choose four rounds, four starting planks, or collecting two planks at a time. Those are rule proposals to compare later.

“We hope they will discuss their plans” is not an achieved result. One person might decide everything while the other follows. So we can keep a question for observation: does each person have opportunities to propose and choose their own actions? Writing down a goal gives later drafts something to check.
What is fixed, and what can change?

Suppose we only have paper and pens, and our table is small. Those are practical conditions. They make a long, three-dimensional river awkward, but do not decide whether players should cooperate or compete. “Both animals must arrive” is the direction we have currently chosen. Shared planks are one possible way to support it; other ways of helping each other could be explored too.

Keeping conditions separate from direction helps us respond to ideas. An electronic bridge that lights up may exceed our available materials. Giving victory only to the first arrival changes whose crossing matters to whom. These proposals affect different parts of the brief, so simply calling either one “good” or “bad” misses the decision involved.

Some limits are temporary ways to get a small piece working. We can start with one route to see how players divide preparation and movement. Once that relationship is clear, we can decide whether a second route helps. Leaving something out for now does not ban it forever.
Use the brief to choose without getting trapped

Suppose we have two ideas: give each animal three hats to wear, or let an animal on the starting bank collect planks for both players. Hats might be enjoyable. But for our current direction, collecting more directly creates the relationship we want: one person’s preparation changes both animals’ journeys. That is a reason to try collecting first, without declaring hats worthless.

The brief can change too. If we later discover that we would rather make a relaxed character-dressing game, we can acknowledge the new direction and reconsider the rules. Trouble comes when the direction changes but we keep judging ideas against an old goal. Asking for tense planning while removing every reason to plan can make successive changes cancel each other out.

“Make a fun game” now has a direction two people can discuss. Use the brief to choose an approach and write an action you can put on the table. After testing, return with specific findings and revise these few sentences.
有了方向，怎样想出不止一种做法？
我们暂定要做一个两人合作过河的纸片游戏：每个人决定自己的动作，同时得顾及同伴。可是，“让玩家合作”还不能告诉我们轮到一个人时，他究竟能做什么。需要把方向往桌面上推近一点。
先想一个具体时刻。小兔到了第一块踏脚石，小刺猬还在岸上；接下来，小刺猬做什么，能影响小兔的处境？它可以取得供双方使用的木板，也可以传递某件东西，或在岸上操作一座桥。这些目前只是候选想法。传递给谁、桥怎样起作用，都还没写清，不能立刻混进基本版。
把同一时刻想成几种不同做法，可以防止我们把最先想到的答案当成唯一答案。随后还得看，每种做法究竟要求增加什么。
从已经知道的东西往外想
构思不一定从一个完整故事开始。手边有纸片，可以想“玩家怎样移动、翻转或分给别人”；已经有河流场景，可以想“过河前要准备什么”；希望两个人互相影响，可以想“一人做什么会改变另一人的选择”。这些入口能够通向同一个设计问题，无须先把整个世界的故事写完。
但只换场景名称，未必产生了新玩法。把“取得木板”叫作“采集魔法叶子”，如果取得条件、数量和用法都相同，玩家作决定时仍面对相同的关系。换名字可能帮助读者理解主题；若我们此刻要找另一种合作方式，就需要继续改变动作或后果。
也可以先把暂时不完整的点子留下。“一人留在岸上准备，另一人先走”已经指出一种互相影响的可能。现在不必立刻给它加天气、道具、角色能力和三种计分。把这些一起加上，会让我们难以看清最初的关系是否成立。
什么时候开始挑选？
产生想法时，过早追问每个细节，会让所有点子都因为“还没写完”而消失。反过来，一直增加点子也不会自动得到可玩的游戏。到了要做第一张纸的时候，就可以把候选放回暂定方向下比较。
以“收集共用木板”和“操作一座桥”为例。前者至少需要可用木板、花过的木板和取得新木板的条件。后者还需要说明桥何时打开、能让谁通过、会不会关闭，以及操作它的人能否离开。这些问题都有可能得到有趣的答案。眼前如果只想先看“谁留下准备”，收集方案已经能把这个关系摆出来，所需说明也更少，因此适合先试。
这不是说规则少的点子永远更好。若目标本来就是两人配合开关桥，桥的这些细节便是要探索的内容。合适的范围来自这次想弄清什么，而不只是数一数有几条规则。
留下一个候选，给它补上能执行的细节
我们于是先选择收集：留在岸上的动物取得木板，双方都能用。它直接连接了个人动作与共同进度。接下来必须追问：只有岸上能收集吗？取得几块？收集后还能移动吗？已经用掉的木板会不会回来？不同答案会形成不同游戏。
基本版选择的是：只在起点收集，每次取得两块新木板，收集用掉这一回合，不能再移动，花掉的木板不再使用。这些条件让留下准备有帮助，也有时间代价。如果可以无限地免费收集，先准备多少就不再是同一种问题。
其他点子先留在候选纸上。这一稿只继续写收集和前进：谁能做、需要什么、完成后留下什么。把这两个动作写清楚，纸上的小动物就能开始过河。
How Can One Direction Lead to Several Ideas?

Our provisional direction is a paper game in which two people cooperate to cross a river. Each controls their own actions while considering their partner. But “make players cooperate” does not tell us what someone can actually do on a turn. We need to bring that direction closer to the table.

Start with a particular moment. Rabbit is on the first stepping stone; Hedgehog is still on the bank. What could Hedgehog do that would affect Rabbit’s situation? Hedgehog might obtain planks both animals can use, pass something along, or operate a bridge from the bank. These are only candidate ideas. We have not decided who can receive an item or how the bridge works, so none of them should silently enter the base game.
Imagining several actions for the same moment helps us avoid treating our first answer as the only answer. Then we can examine what each proposal would require.
Expand from something you already have

An idea does not have to begin with a complete story. With paper pieces in hand, we can ask how players might move, turn over, or share them. With a river setting, we can ask what needs preparing before a crossing. If we want two people to affect each other, we can ask what one person could do to change the other’s choices. These starting points can lead toward the same design problem without requiring a whole fictional world first.

Changing names alone may leave the play unchanged. If “collecting planks” becomes “gathering magical leaves,” but the conditions, quantities, and uses stay the same, players still face the same decisions. A new name may help communicate the theme. To find a different way of cooperating, we need to change an action or its consequences too.

We can also keep an idea before every detail is settled. “One animal prepares on the bank while the other moves ahead” already suggests a useful relationship. It does not immediately need weather, items, special powers, and three kinds of scoring. Adding all those things at once would make the original relationship harder to examine.
When should you start choosing?

During idea generation, demanding every detail too early can eliminate everything for being unfinished. Yet collecting more ideas indefinitely will not produce a playable game either. When we are ready to make the first paper draft, we can compare candidates against our provisional direction.

Consider shared plank collection and operating a bridge. Collection needs available planks, spent planks, and conditions for obtaining new ones. A bridge needs rules for when it opens, who can cross, whether it closes again, and whether the operator can leave. Those questions might have interesting answers. If our immediate question is simply “who stays behind to prepare?”, collecting already makes that relationship visible with fewer things to explain. That makes it a useful first candidate.

Fewer rules are not always better. If our goal were coordinating a bridge’s opening and closing, those details would be the very things we needed to explore. The useful scope depends on the question, not merely the number of rules.
Give the chosen idea details people can carry out

So we start with collecting: an animal on the bank obtains planks that either animal can use. This directly connects an individual action to shared progress. Now we must ask: can animals collect only on the bank? How many planks do they get? Can they move afterward? Do spent planks return? Different answers create different games.

The base game chooses these answers: collect only on the starting bank, obtain two new planks, use the whole turn to collect, and never reuse spent planks. These conditions make preparation helpful while giving it a cost in time. Unlimited free collection would create a different planning problem.

Keep the other ideas on their own sheets. This draft continues with collecting and moving: who can do each, what it needs, and what it leaves behind. With those actions written, the paper animals can begin crossing.
“让动物过河”，要变成哪些动作？
“帮助小动物过河”说明了我们希望完成什么，还没有说明玩家怎样做。拿起小兔放到对岸，也算把它送过河，却绕开了整个游戏。设计动作，要把故事里的愿望变成桌上允许发生的变化。
我们先做一份可以直接运行的基本版纸上草稿，再看看每个动作为什么要写这些细节。它只需要画线、写字和移动纸片，外观可以在规则清楚以后继续修改。
把一局需要的东西摆出来
纸上画四个位置，依次连接：起点河岸、第一块踏脚石、第二块踏脚石、对岸。另做小兔和小刺猬两张动物纸片、二十张木板纸片，以及一个用来指示第几轮的标记。写出“第1轮”到“第4轮”，把标记放在第1轮。再写一个先指向小林的回合提示，避免忘记轮到谁。
小林控制小兔，小雨控制小刺猬，两只都放在起点。二十张木板中，四张放在中央的“可用木板”区，十六张放在另一个“备用纸片”区；旁边再留出空的“已用木板”区。备用纸片表示还没取得的新木板，和已经花过的木板分开。
